title: John Chartier’s silver coffee pot
dimensions: Overall: 24.6 x 15.3 x 15 cm (9 11/16 x 6 x 5 7/8 in.); Diameter of base: 11 cm (4 5/16 in.)
feature: a separate wooden handle
fact: Cleveland credits John Chartier with fabricating the 1702 silver coffee pot and identifies its wooden handle.
limit: The handle material can guide a separate contact probe. Neither the date nor the material gives a measured cooling curve.
alt: Tall silver pot with narrow spout, domed lid and side handle.

title: Sixte-Simon Rion’s covered chocolate pot
feature: a side-mounted wooden handle
fact: Cleveland credits Sixte-Simon Rion for the covered silver chocolate pot with a wooden side handle.
limit: A hand contact and a metal body have separate readings. No original serving temperature is recorded here.
alt: Cylindrical metal pot with a lid and a dark handle projecting sideways.

title: Berlin porcelain chocolate pot
feature: a flared porcelain body
fact: Cleveland records a late eighteenth-century porcelain chocolate pot from the Royal Porcelain Manufactory in Berlin.
limit: The catalogue supplies material and maker. The model chooses where the replica touches the support.
alt: Pale lidded porcelain pot with a rounded belly and painted pink decoration.

title: Louis Rorimer’s coffee pot
feature: a dark ebony grip beside the silver body
fact: Cleveland credits Louis Rorimer for the design and the Rokesley Shop for making it. The record lists silver, moonstones and ebony.
limit: The named collaboration identifies responsibility for design and making. The hand-contact trial belongs to the replica.
alt: Tall angular silver-colored pot with a long spout and dark loop handle.

title: Glazed stoneware coffee pot, possibly Namur
material: glazed stoneware with silver colored metal mounts
feature: the contrast between the dark body and metal mounts
fact: Cleveland records a glazed stoneware body with silver-colored metal mounts and gives Namur as a possible origin.
limit: Silver-colored describes appearance in this record. It leaves the mount’s alloy and measured conductivity open.
alt: Dark lidded coffee pot with a raised handle and shiny metal-colored mounts.

title: Niderviller covered cream jug
material: hard-paste porcelain with enamel and gilt decoration
feature: the foot and lidded porcelain body
fact: Cleveland credits the Niderviller Factory for this covered cream jug and identifies hard-paste porcelain and enamel and gilt decoration.
limit: The covered shape is useful for the contact stand model. The trial does not establish that this jug held hot cream.
alt: Footed cream jug with decoration beneath its domed lid.

title: Sèvres cream jug with two dates
feature: the narrow foot under the porcelain well
fact: Cleveland dates the design to 1788 and the making of this Sèvres cream jug to 1831–34. The catalogue identifies gilt porcelain.
limit: The two dates refer to different acts. Use only the replica to compare contact and retained warmth.
alt: Green and gold porcelain cream jug with a raised grip and narrow base.

title: Fabergé covered hot water pot
feature: the gilt silver body with separate enamel decoration
fact: Cleveland credits the House of Fabergé as maker and attributes the workmaster role to Feodor Ivanovich Rückert. It lists gilt silver and opaque cloisonné enamel.
limit: The museum identifies enamel on metal. A decorated surface alone gives no hand-contact reading.
alt: Covered multicolored pot with floral enamel and curving spout.

title: Seifū Yohei III’s teapot with pines
dimensions: height with lid: 8 cm (3 1/8 in.); width with handle: 10.5 cm (4 1/8 in.); Diameter: 8 cm (3 1/8 in.)
feature: a porcelain body at the side grip
fact: Cleveland names Seifū Yohei III for this blue underglaze porcelain teapot. The record describes the use of the side-handled kyūsu form for steeping and serving.
limit: Use the particular documented shape. The toy fixture supplies the contact point and the interval.
alt: Round white porcelain teapot with underglaze blue pine design.

title: John Edwards’s hot water jug and stand
catalogueTitle: Hot Water Jug with Hinged Cover
dimensions: Average: 17.2 cm (6 3/4 in.); Container: 21.3 x 20 cm (8 3/8 x 7 7/8 in.); stand: 8.4 x 10.9 cm (3 5/16 x 4 5/16 in.)
feature: a hinged cover and separate stand
fact: Cleveland describes the 1800 silver hot water jug with a hinged lid and credits John Edwards. Its stand has a component record under the same accession.
limit: The stand can be discussed separately from the jug. Its original service interval is unknown.
alt: Tall silver-colored water jug with a curved side handle and hinged lid.

title: Muromachi iron kettle with crane design
dimensions: Diameter: 30.4 cm (11 15/16 in.); Diameter of mouth: 18.6 cm (7 5/16 in.); Overall: 18.2 cm (7 3/16 in.); with handle: 31.5 cm (12 3/8 in.)
feature: a broad cast iron body
fact: Cleveland places this iron kettle in the Muromachi period and documents its crane design and water-heating context.
limit: The comparison uses the underside and a toy contact pad. It leaves historical fuel, heating time and handling open.
alt: Low dark iron kettle with a broad rim and a lid.

title: Edo covered iron tea kettle
feature: the raised handle above the iron body
fact: Cleveland identifies the covered tea kettle as iron and places it in the Edo period. The catalogue records the lid with the vessel.
limit: The distance to the raised handle is visible. The original temperature at that handle remains unknown.
alt: Decorated iron kettle with a tall loop over the lid.

title: Chinese bronze kettle with handle
place: China, Qing attribution or Republican period in the record
feature: the bronze body and supported foot
fact: Cleveland records bronze for the lidded kettle and gives a 1700s–1800s date and lists period alternatives.
limit: Preserve the catalogue’s alternatives. A bench mock-up supplies the thermal behaviour.
alt: Round dark bronze kettle with feet and a handle over its lid.

title: Nathaniel Hurd’s silver and wood teapot
dimensions: with handle: 14.5 x 24.4 cm (5 11/16 x 9 5/8 in.)
feature: wood at the grip and separate engraved silver
fact: Cleveland names Nathaniel Hurd as maker. It identifies silver and wood and describes the engraved Gibbs family arms.
limit: The engraved side supplies identification. Contact behaviour depends on which model surface touches the probe.
alt: Polished oval silver pot with a curved brown wooden grip.

title: Seifū Yohei IV’s teapot with bamboo
material: Porcelain with underglaze blue, molded design and metal handles
dimensions: with handle: 16 cm (6 5/16 in.); Lid: 0.5 x 7 cm (3/16 x 2 3/4 in.); width with spout: 14.5 cm (5 11/16 in.)
feature: separate metal handles and a porcelain body
fact: Cleveland names Seifū Yohei IV and lists a porcelain body with molded design, underglaze blue and metal handles.
limit: The handle and vessel can use different materials. The numerical contrast refers to the stand-in.
alt: White pot with blue bamboo decoration and a raised metal loop.

title: Indian silver teapot
feature: a patterned silver foot and side grip
fact: Cleveland records a nineteenth-century silver teapot made in India and discusses export or a British colonial clientele as alternatives.
limit: Both possible markets stay on the note. The actual user and the object’s cooling behavior remain open.
alt: Wide-patterned silver teapot with narrow foot, long spout and curved handle.

title: Chen Hanwen’s Yixing teapot with an imperial poem
catalogueTitle: Teapot with Landscape and Imperial Poem
material: Stoneware, with gold pigment, Yixing ware
dimensions: Diameter: 10.8 cm (4 1/4 in.); Overall: 7.5 cm (2 15/16 in.); with spout: 15 cm (5 7/8 in.)
feature: the polished stoneware wall below the inscription
fact: Cleveland credits Chen Hanwen for the Yixing teapot and identifies a poem by the Qianlong emperor on one side.
limit: The poem’s composition and the pot’s material are separate records. The model gives no original use temperature.
alt: Rounded polished brown teapot with gold pigment and two short projecting forms.

title: Aaron Wood’s modeled Staffordshire teapot
dimensions: Overall: 14.6 x 18.8 cm (5 3/4 x 7 3/8 in.); Container: 11.5 cm (4 1/2 in.)
feature: the angular salt-glazed body
fact: Cleveland lists the Staffordshire Factory for making the salt-glazed earthenware and Aaron Wood for modeling it.
limit: The glaze and molded form are documented. Use the shape to choose the position of the toy contact probe.
alt: Angular lidded pale teapot with straight sides and raised ornament.

title: Davenport black basalt teapot
dimensions: Diameter of mouth: 11.8 cm (4 5/8 in.); Overall: 10.6 x 23.5 cm (4 3/16 x 9 1/4 in.)
feature: the dark body and ribbed foot
fact: Cleveland credits the Davenport Pottery and Porcelain Factory and names the material black basalt.
limit: Keep the museum’s ceramic name. The dark colour gives no direct temperature reading.
alt: Dark matt teapot with a ribbed body and a loop handle.

title: Wedgwood stoneware teapot
feature: the raised pattern on a stoneware body
fact: Cleveland assigns the c. 1830 stoneware teapot to the Wedgwood Factory. The decorated body provides the contact placement for the replica.
limit: The factory and material are recorded. The historic pace of service remains unknown.
alt: Cream teapot with a silver-toned highlight, raised pattern and lidded top.

title: Chinese export porcelain teapot
feature: the pale porcelain wall and loop
fact: Cleveland places the porcelain teapot in Chinese export production for the European market. It records a date around 1750–1770.
limit: An intended market does not identify an individual buyer. The replica supplies the load and wait.
alt: Pale round teapot with dark painted decoration and a loop handle.

title: Chantilly porcelain teapot
feature: a lidded soft-paste porcelain wall
fact: Cleveland credits Chantilly Porcelain Factory and documents Japanese prototypes for the shapes and decoration of this set.
limit: A prototype can circulate while a particular piece is made elsewhere. Keep its material separate from the pattern.
alt: Round lidded porcelain teapot with painted color and a long pale loop.

title: Parcel-gilt silver coffee pot
feature: a fluted silver body under the narrow neck
fact: The Met dates the parcel-gilt silver coffee pot to 1809–60 and lists Turkey as its geography.
limit: Only parts of the surface are gilt. The museum entry supplies no measured warming curve.
alt: Tall silver coffee pot with a narrow neck and fluted lower body.

title: Copper coffee pot catalogued to Yarkand or Tashkent
place: Yarkand or Tashkent, China or present-day Uzbekistan in the catalogue
feature: an embossed, chased copper surface
fact: The Met records copper, worked in relief and chased, and keeps both proposed places in the entry.
limit: The surface marks leave manufacture uncertain between the recorded alternatives. Keep the practice trace separate.
alt: Tall metal coffee pot with a pointed lid and curved ornamented profile.

title: Brass teapot with applied copper
feature: the brass body and applied copper
fact: The Met describes a brass teapot with applied copper and gives its eighteenth-century date as probable.
limit: Two named metals do not make the same contact. The model does not report the mixture or composition of the originals.
alt: Dark bulbous metal teapot with different-colored raised elements near the spout and grip.

title: Shi Dabin’s plum-blossom teapot
catalogueTitle: Teapot in the Shape of a Plum Blossom
feature: the shaped stoneware body
fact: The Met credits Shi Dabin for this early seventeenth-century Yixing stoneware teapot shaped as a plum blossom.
limit: The distinctive shape identifies the object without fixing a serving count or original temperature.
alt: Small red-brown stoneware teapot with ridges around the sides.

title: Eighteenth-century jade teapot
feature: a carved jade vessel and lid
fact: The Met records a Chinese teapot in jade with three pieces under the same accession.
limit: The material and title leave the original service of this object open. The heat pulse belongs to its teaching model.
alt: Pale carved jade vessel with a raised lid and sculpted side elements.

title: Aoki Mokubei’s Kyoto-ware teapot
material: Faience decorated with design in relief and glaze (Kyoto ware)
feature: a side handle and glazed faience body
fact: The Met credits Aoki Mokubei for the dated teapot and describes relief and glaze on faience.
limit: The relief is a documented surface property. The probe gives a new reading on a plain part of the replica.
alt: Round textured lidded teapot with a long thick side handle.

title: Kitei’s Kyoto-ware teapot
material: White porcelain decorated with blue under the glaze (Kyoto ware)
feature: blue beneath the glaze of a white porcelain body
fact: The Met names Kitei for the covered teapot from 1860 and describes decoration in blue beneath the glaze.
limit: The glaze position and the maker are recorded. The fitting exercise uses its own probe and wait.
alt: Pale covered blue-decorated teapot with a curved side handle.

title: German milk-glass teapot
feature: a glass body beneath the opaque surface
fact: The Met classifies this c. 1750 covered teapot as milk glass.
limit: The opaque color can look ceramic. Use the documented material rather than the color when setting the separate hand-contact probe.
alt: Opaque white lidded teapot with dark decoration and a pale handle.

title: Blue molded glass cream jug
material: Blown molded lead blue and colorless glass
feature: a differently colored grip beside the blown glass body
fact: The Met identifies blown molded blue lead glass and colorless glass for the 1820–40 jug.
limit: The jug’s medium supports a glass model. It records no temperature for a historical serving.
alt: Deep-blue cream jug with a clear curled loop handle.

title: Roswell Gleason’s coffee urn
feature: pewter, brass and wood on a tall urn
fact: The Met credits Roswell Gleason as maker and records pewter, brass and wood. The tall urn is held with its separate lid.
limit: A catalogue names multiple materials. The contact test uses one fixture at a time to avoid confusing them.
alt: Tall metal urn with a stemmed foot, lidded top and two side handles.

title: William Kirby’s pewter and wood teapot
feature: a wooden grip separated from pewter
fact: The Met names William Kirby as maker and records pewter and wood for the teapot.
limit: The metal and wood survive in one object. Neither specifies how many intervals a historical delivery took.
alt: Pewter pot with a rounded tiered body and a dark handle.

title: Harmanus Nieuwenhuys’s covered teapot
feature: silver and wood on a lidded body
fact: The Met credits Harmanus Nieuwenhuys and records silver and wood for the covered teapot dated 1743.
limit: The documented wood supports a buffered grip in the model. Real thermal performance remains unmeasured.
alt: Silver-colored decorated pot with a dark serpentine loop handle.

title: Moscow teapot catalogued with Al’derman Petrov Fiodor
feature: a round silver body and a separate wooden grip
fact: The Met records 1765 and credits Al’derman Petrov Fiodor in the maker field for the combined silver and wood teapot.
limit: The figure on the catalogue tag identifies the maker credit. The mock-up’s materials give only a training contrast.
alt: Rounded metal teapot with decoration on the belly and a dark loop grip.

title: Pierre Vallières’s silver chocolate pot
feature: a side grip fitted to the silver body
fact: The Met credits Pierre Vallières for this silver and wood chocolate pot dated 1781.
limit: The documented material leaves original contents and hand-contact conditions open.
alt: Tall silver pot on feet with a dark shaped side grip.

title: Meissen porcelain chocolate pot with wood and mounts
feature: gilt bronze mounts between porcelain and wood
fact: The Met credits the Meissen Manufactory and lists hard-paste porcelain, gilt bronze and wood.
limit: The documented join links different materials. The fixture tracks where its probe touches each model.
alt: Pale turquoise lidded pot with a long dark side handle and gilt mount.

title: David King’s silver and wood teapot
feature: a wooden grip on a low silver pot
fact: The Met credits David King and dates the silver and wood teapot to 1723–24.
limit: Its low form can guide the training cradle. The model records its own pulse and elapsed intervals.
alt: Low oval silver teapot with a dark curved wooden grip.
